changes.old: \caption{Comparison of KL and DW pointwise probability acceptance regions for common illustrative parameters $N^{\mathrm{te}}=100$, $\theta=3$, and $s=\nu=1$. Blue denotes the KL region; blue and gold together denote the DW region. The inset magnifies the left tail. Solid blue and dashed gold boundaries are obtained by numerical inversion; the dotted line is $p=q$. Continuous acceptance envelopes are shown, with empirical CDF levels restricted to $j/N^{\mathrm{te}}$.}
changes.new: \caption{\textbf{KL and DW acceptance regions.} Blue denotes KL acceptance; gold adds probabilities accepted only by DW. The inset magnifies the left tail. Boundaries are computed numerically using the illustrative parameters shown; $q$ is displayed continuously between empirical levels $j/N^{\mathrm{te}}$.}

changes.old: \caption{Illustration of simultaneous confidence bounds across response thresholds. The shaded region represents the simultaneous confidence band for the true response CDF $p_f(c)$, bounded by $\underline p_{\hat f}(c)$ and $\overline p_{\hat f}(c)$. The highlighted vertical segment at $c=0$ corresponds to the original confidence interval for the failure probability.}
changes.new: \caption{\textbf{Simultaneous confidence band.} Blue shading bounds the response CDF $p_f(c)$; the gold segment at $c=0$ is the original failure probability interval.}

changes.old: \caption{Illustration of the residual and input-threshold partitions for $K=3$. The residual partition consists of $K$ singleton cells and $K+1$ open intervals, whereas the input partition is induced by half-open intervals of the failure threshold $-\hat g(\bm x)$. Here, $w_i=\mathbb P(\mathcal X_i)$ denotes the probability mass of input cell $\mathcal X_i$.}
changes.new: \caption{\textbf{Residual and input partitions.} For $K=3$, three singletons and four open intervals partition $\Xi$. Half-open intervals of $-\hat g(\bm x)$ induce the input cells, with masses $w_i=\mathbb P(\mathcal X_i)$.}

changes.old: \caption{Joint partition of the input and residual spaces for $K=3$. Each product cell has probability mass $\pi_{ij}=\Pi(\mathcal X_i\times\Xi_j)$. The blue, yellow, and red cells correspond to $(\underline h_{ij},\overline h_{ij})=(0,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(1,1)$, respectively.}
changes.new: \caption{\textbf{Joint cell partition.} For $K=3$, each cell has mass $\pi_{ij}=\Pi(\mathcal X_i\times\Xi_j)$. Blue, gold, and red denote safe, overlap, and failure cells, respectively.}
